text.p: Africa's leading oil producer Nigeria was gripped by a fuel shortage on Thursday for a third day running as vehicles jammed petrol stations, motorists said.
It was the fifth fuel shortage in the commercial capital Lagos this year.
"I came to the petrol station at dawn but until now I haven't got any fuel," said one cab driver. "This is a shame for an oil-producing nation."
Fuel shortages are common in Nigeria, where poor management has reduced output of its four oil refineries to a third of their combined total capacity of 445,000 barrels per day.
As a result Nigeria has often had to import fuel.
The latest shortage caused traffic chaos in Lagos, a metropolis of six million people, as long queues formed by vehicles at pumping stations spilled onto the roads.
Thousands of commuters were stranded along major roads while commercial buses and taxis doubled fares.
"It was difficult getting a taxi this morning and I had to pay 60 naira ($0.70) instead of 30 naira to reach my office," grumbled banker John Chibuzor, who works in central Lagos.
State-run oil company NNPC officials were not available to comment but the semi-official Daily Times newspaper said the shortage was due to delays in discharging oil products from a ship.

"A vessel carrying 19,000 tonnes of fuel has been delayed by immigration officials because two of its crew had no valid papers," one official was quoted as saying, adding that the matter had been resolved and the situation should improve.

Earlier in the week industry sources, citing a dispute between Petroleum Tanker Drivers' Association and the National Association of Road Transport Owners, warned of disruption in fuel distribution in the run-up to Easter holidays.
There has been no comment from the unions.
The independent Guardian newspaper said the fuel shortages had spread to nearby Osun state.
